evidence.reason: Frame-size heuristic is not a sound test for an xpcall frame; non-xpcall frames can pass it, yielding a bogus errfunc stack slot.

verdict.summary: This is the patched glibc glob() implementation. The historically vulnerable spots (GLOB_TILDE one-byte overflow BZ#22320, GLOB_TILDE unescape overflow CVE-2017-15804, GLOB_BRACE onealt sizing, gl_offs/gl_pathv size overflow) all contain their corrective guards: exact-fit allocation sizes, SIZE_MAX/sizeof(char*) overflow checks, and the 'filename == NULL' condition on the trailing-backslash re-emission. All allocation failures are checked and stop execution; dirname ownership flags prevent double free.

evidence.reason: &dirname[1] contributes exactly dirlen bytes (dirlen-1 chars + NUL), so the allocation is an exact fit, not a one-byte underallocation.
CVE-2017-15804 fix present: the backslash is only re-emitted when the whole pattern is the tilde expression, keeping writes within the end_name-dirname sized buffer.
Prevents integer overflow in the (newcount+2)*sizeof(char*) realloc size.

assumptions: next_brace_sub, glob_in_dir, prefix_array, scratch_buffer_* behave per standard glibc contracts

evidence.reason: Indexing the recursion bitmap by an unbounded, attacker-influenced recursion depth; the only guard (PAREN_TEST on the previous level) prevents repeating the same paren but not increasing depth through distinct parens.

assumptions: RExC_study_chunk_recursed is allocated for a limited number of depth levels, as in Perl's regcomp.c.
limitations: Allocation site of RExC_study_chunk_recursed not shown; exact level capacity inferred from upstream code.
